key_insight: A matrix-free FFT solver combines scaled boundary finite elements with a Fourier-space preconditioner to deliver stable voxel-based elastic homogenization without the excessive stiffness of fully integrated elements.
engineering_relevance: The method supports effective-property prediction for porous and highly heterogeneous materials while accommodating arbitrary stiffness anisotropy.
method: Discretize a regular periodic voxel grid with hexahedral SBFEM cells, using analytical radial solutions.
Apply a homogeneous SBFEM stiffness-based preconditioner locally in Fourier space.
Avoid global stiffness-matrix storage, with a preconditioned condition-number bound governed by material contrast rather than grid resolution.
evidence_signal: Tests on a short-fibre composite, polyurethane foam, and a sand-based binder jet microstructure show robust convergence and competitive accuracy, including stability where reduced-integration elements become unstable.
watch_item: The stated condition-number bound depends on material contrast; grid-resolution independence alone does not guarantee contrast-independent convergence.
paper_title: Scaled boundary finite elements for FFT-based computational micromechanics
